Both name the exact same defect: startPeek/peekIdentity in cmd/configserver/main.go add a backLink parameter and --back-link flag not present in the peek-multiple-profiles plan's approved signature (plans/v1-2-1/2026-08-30-peek-multiple-profiles-wip-78bfb3e/design/change-multi-profile-ports.md), an undocumented deviation from the binding plan contract.

SP-002's 'Bash detection only catches the exact two-word cat <path> shape' restates GV3-166's bullet (2): the hook's Bash-path detection matches only the exact bare 'cat <path>' token form, so any other read invocation (head, cat -n, less, python3 -c, etc.) is invisible to the tokenizer and bypasses the ctx-dir read block.

uncataloged.reason: CheckPolicy (internal/acdsl/policy.go:329-336): when policyBase() cannot resolve ANY base ref (baseErr != nil, e.g. base_ref set to a nonexistent ref), CheckPolicy checks policy.Mode == PolicyModeFree using the raw, untrusted working-tree policy argument BEFORE ever calling basePolicy() to fetch/validate the committed base policy — so {"mode":"free","base_ref":"nosuchref"} in the working copy makes CheckPolicy return (nil,nil) regardless of the base branch's real gated/strict policy. Verified in code: `if baseErr != nil { if policy.Mode == PolicyModeFree { return nil, nil } ... }` at policy.go:331-335 — the `policy` here is the function's own untrusted parameter, never replaced by basePolicy()'s result on this path. This is a genuine 4th distinct bypass mechanism in the same function alongside the cataloged GV3-001 (resolvable base lacking policy.json -> basePolicy fallback -> free short-circuit), GV3-002 (base_ref=branch -> isBoundary false) and GV4-202 (base_ref=HEAD -> vacuous diff) — none of which cover an unresolvable base_ref combined with an explicit free mode. The closest golden hit, GV3-108 (INFO), lists this same branch ("CheckPolicy free+unresolvable-base") only as an untested/unexercised edge case, not as an identified security bypass — a different root-cause characterization (test-coverage gap vs. exploitable gate bypass), so it does not cover SP-001's claim.

install.sh:173-178 (the new peek-port stale-kill loop, `for peek_port in "$PEEK_PORT" "$PEEK_CONTROL_PORT"; do pid="$(lsof -tiTCP:"$peek_port" -sTCP:LISTEN || true)"; ... kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; ...`) passes lsof's output as a single quoted argument to kill; if more than one PID is listening on the port, "$pid" is a multi-line non-numeric string, kill fails, and the failure is swallowed by `|| true` with no operator-visible signal, leaving a stale peek process running. Verified in the reviewed diff at exactly those lines. The only golden entry at these same lines, GV3-148 (NIT), flags a different defect entirely — that this new block is a near-verbatim duplicate of the pre-existing $ADDR_PORT block a few lines above — not the multi-PID silent-failure bug SP-003 identifies. No golden entry covers this functional defect.
